"That's a secret. A military secret." Military secret is not a "yes". And not a "no". It leaves us hanging. And that, I suspect, is the point. stories.article_text_excerpt: Russia is raising utility tariffs for the second time this year, with an average 15% increase taking effect on 1 October — a move the central bank says will push inflation further above its target in an economy already under severe pressure from war costs and sanctions.The increase will range from 8% to 22% depending on the region. Residents of Stavropol Krai, Dagestan, and the Tambov and Tyumen regions face the steepest rises, while Moscow tariffs will go up 15% and St Petersburg 14.6%.An earlier 1.7% increase took effect in January. stories.summary: Bank of America executive Erin Piacenti has been named as the victim killed in New York by a woman who stabbed two people in Times Square before being fatally shot by police. The woman has reportedly had a history of mental health issues, according to the NYPD.
stories.article_text_excerpt: A woman randomly stabbed two people in New York City’s Times Square on Monday, killing one woman, and then was fatally shot by police, according to officials.The shooting happened just before 4:30 pm local time, next to a New York Police Department (NYPD) substation, just outside One Times Square, the building that hosts the city’s annual New Year’s Eve ball drop celebration. It is one of the most heavily touristed and policed spots in all of New York.The 49-year-old woman from Queens pulled out two knives from a shopping bag and stabbed a 68-year-old man who had just come out of the subway station and was waiting to cross the street with his wife, striking him in the abdomen, Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at a news conference.Seconds later, the woman stabbed a 32-year-old woman also in the abdomen, Tisch said. Both victims were taken to the hospital. The woman died and the man is in stable condition, according to police.Police didn’t say if the victims were tourists visiting the city or residents. stories.summary: The UN Secretary-General told Euronews in Bishkek that some of the key actors in wars in the Middle East and Ukraine were in the room with him, and that it was time to "stop the madness".

stories.article_text_excerpt: A cargo ship sank in the Marmara Sea near Istanbul after colliding with a second vessel, with rescuers searching for 10 people who were on board, Turkish officials said on Wednesday.The incident occurred before dawn when the ALSU, an empty oil tanker, collided with the Tuğberk İmamoğlu, a cargo ship carrying rolled steel, which sank shortly after, the transport ministry's maritime directorate said on X.The collision occurred 18 nautical miles (33 kilometres) off the Silivri district on the western edge of Istanbul province, the governor's office said on X."Due to the Tuğberk İmamoğlu not responding to any calls and the crew not answering their mobile phones...it is believed the dry cargo ship has sunk," the maritime directorate said.The ALSU's captain had reported the collision as happening at 3:15 am, with 14 search and rescue vessels dispatched to the area backed by a helicopter, it said."Life-saving equipment, including a lifeboat belonging to the Tuğberk İmamoğlu which had 10 crew members on board, has been found at sea. stories.title: Algerian president seeks to impose death penalty on arsonists
stories.summary: Algeria declared three days of mourning after wildfires killed 12 people and injured dozens. Authorities said 46 fires remained active, with 54 people hospitalised for burns, including six in critical condition.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune is seeking to reinstate the death penalty for arsonists following deadly wildfires that have ravaged parts of the country.Tebboune declared three days of national mourning on Thursday after wildfires in the northeast of the country killed at least 12 people and injured dozens more.In a statement, Tebboune described the loss of life as "a great tragedy," as officials maintained the official death toll from Wednesday.Algeria has observed a moratorium on the death penalty since 1993, but the Algerian head of state has ordered that "an amendment to the Criminal Code" be made by 15 September.12 people died, 54 in hospitalInterior Minister Saïd Sayoud confirmed five fatalities in Jijel province, four in Béjaïa, and three in Tizi Ouzou following the outbreak of the fires. stories.title: Fake goods, real danger: the €83 billion business behind Europe's illicit trade
stories.summary: A hidden network of organised crime is flooding European markets with counterfeit goods worth billions, and investigators warn that consumers are unknowingly funding it.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Nearly 5% of goods entering the EU are fake, costing businesses an estimated €83 billion annually. At the port of Alicante, OLAF and Spanish Customs officers sift through shipping containers, hunting for counterfeit products hidden in plain sight among legitimate trade. Experts describe illicit trade as a sophisticated global business model, no longer limited to luxury items but now spanning car parts, electronics, pharmaceuticals and food. Counterfeit car components pose particular risks, as they bypass safety testing entirely. Officials stress that buying fakes helps finance serious crimes, including drug and human trafficking, urging shoppers to think twice before chasing a bargain.
